audit.dimension: Freehand drawing canvas (the core Scribbl mechanic)
audit.summary: Buiy has NO paintable/immediate-mode drawing surface and no way to present a freehand-drawn image inside its widget tree. Its render pipeline is a closed set of typed primitives (Quad, Shadow, Glyph, and a placeholder Path that just falls back to the quad shader — crates/buiy_core/src/render/buckets.rs:35-45, primitive.rs:226-233); there is no polyline/stroke/path GPU primitive, no ImageNode/texture-presenting node, and no custom-material/custom-shader/custom-draw escape hatch on a node. A lyon-based stroke tessellator exists but ONLY to bake ~25 STATIC SVG icons once into a content-addressed atlas (icon_raster.rs), not a per-frame paint path. examples/capture does render-to-texture, but via raw Bevy (Camera2d -> RenderTarget -> Readback of the whole Buiy scene) with no Buiy node able to consume a texture. The only in-tree way to draw is "one rotated quad node per stroke segment" — geometrically supported (affine + absolute pos) but perf-fatal: adding a node trips a Full re-extract + full instance re-upload (512 nodes already = 45 ms/frame). The 2026-06-25 audit confirms Media/images/Canvas2D are "Zero code". A drawing canvas is a net-new framework subsystem, not app-level work.

verdict.correction: Both halves of the claimed gap exist and ship in production. title: Arbitrary vector shapes (timer ring, avatars, spinner)

audit.dimension: Arbitrary vector shapes (timer ring, avatars, spinner)
audit.summary: The GPU can draw a fixed primitive set: rounded-rect quads (fill + corner radius + rotation/scale via a per-instance 2D affine), per-side border/outline "band" rings, drop shadows (blurred quad), and linear + radial gradients — all quad-family, all rotatable. Text/icons paint on a separate "coverage" tier (monochrome R8 in a glyph atlas, alpha-as-color tint). Crucially, Buiy already ships a REAL arbitrary-vector path capability: the `Icon` component takes a raw SVG `d` string (M/L/H/V/C/S/Q/T/A/Z, abs+rel, arcs flattened), tessellates it with lyon (stroke w/ round cap+join, or nonzero fill), rasterizes to R8 coverage, and content-addresses it into the glyph atlas — so any static path (circle, ring, arc, avatar face) renders today. The hard limits: the coverage tier (glyphs+icons) drops rotation entirely (only translation is applied), there is no stroke-dasharray / conic / sweep primitive, icons are single-tint monochrome, and every distinct path string is a fresh lyon+raster+atlas cell (no dynamic-geometry channel; the reserved `Path` GPU primitive is an unbuilt placeholder).

1) Icon is single-tint (claim verified). crates/buiy_core/src/render/components.rs:272-290 — the Icon component has exactly ONE field `color: ColorToken` (line 289); no Vec of fills, no per-path palette. icon_producer.rs:321-332 emits exactly one GlyphAlphaInstance per Icon entity (IconEntityRun doc line 71-73: "v1 emits exactly one icon instance per Icon entity"), tinted by a single resolve_token(&icon.color) (line 261). icon_raster.rs:254-270 rasterizes to a single-channel R8 CoverageR8 bitmap (alpha-as-color), IconPaint is Stroke|Fill only (lines 62-69). The atlas key hashes (path_d, stroke_width, size, fill) — no color in the key (line 103), because color rides the instance, i.e. strictly one color slot per instance.

2) No user-facing image/texture/sprite/avatar content primitive anywhere. grep for `pub struct .*Image|ImageNode|Sprite|Avatar|Picture|Handle<Image>` across crates+examples returns ONLY internal render-target/atlas plumbing: tests/support/mod.rs:426/664 (render_to_image/readback_rgba), render/atlas/page.rs:14 (atlas page Handle<Image>), render/golden.rs:260 (capture_to_image). No content-image widget or component. buiy_widgets/src has button/checkbox/dialog/disclosure/menu/popover/slider/switch/text_input/tooltip — NO avatar, badge, or image widget (grep avatar|badge|image|sprite → 0 hits).

3) Color emoji is explicitly NAMED-BUT-NOT-BUILT, which reinforces (not refutes) the gap. text/extract.rs:874,892,941-943,1049-1052 — SwashContent::Color glyphs hit ResolveAction::SkipColorEmoji and are skipped with a warn_once ("color (emoji) glyphs are skipped in v1 — the ColorRgba8/IconInstance seam"). So a multi-color emoji "little face" would NOT render either.

4) The Path primitive kind is bucket-RESERVED but UNIMPLEMENTED. render/buckets.rs:35-55 defines BuiyPrimitiveKind::Path ("Filled arbitrary 2D path SDF"); render/primitive.rs:231 maps Path => shader_handle() i.e. it "falls back to the quad shader as a placeholder" (primitive.rs:225). No extract-side Path producer exists (grep Path=>/IconInstance/ColorRgba8 in extract.rs → 0). Even if built, it is described as a single filled SDF path = single fill.

5) The ONLY multi-color-within-one-primitive facility is gradients (LinearGradient/RadialGradient, components.rs:99/133 with Vec<ColorStop>), but the GPU path is a 2-stop smooth RAMP (extract.rs:286 "Two-stop fast path", 300; components.rs:93-95 "design uses 2 stops... B1 GPU fast path is 2 stops"). A smooth 2-stop ramp across a box is not "multi-fill per path" and cannot render an arbitrary multi-color avatar/face.

Conclusion: the only way to draw a multi-color shape today is the exact workaround the gap already states — stack N single-color Icons/quads (or gradient-fill boxes). No existing API/primitive/widget/component provides multi-fill-per-path or a raster-image primitive to sidestep it. Correction: empty (genuinely missing).

CONFIRMED. Searched the whole tree (crates/buiy_core, buiy_widgets, buiy, buiy_bsn, buiy_verify, all examples) for tween/animat/Lerp/interpolat/easing/progress/sweep and every `*Tween` type.

(1) Exhaustive target enumeration: the ONLY tween-target component types in the entire repo are exactly five, each hard-bound to one concrete component — crates/buiy_core/src/animation/tween.rs:249 TranslateTween→Translate, :253 RotateTween→Rotate, :257 ScaleTween→Scale, :261 OpacityTween→Opacity, :266 BackgroundColorTween→AnimatedBackgroundColor. `grep -roE '[A-Za-z]+Tween'` over crates/ + examples/ returns only these five; no other struct ending in `Tween` is defined anywhere. The lone f32 system, advance_opacity_tweens (tween.rs), hard-writes `Opacity(v)` — there is no system that advances a bare `Tween<f32>` on a user component and writes it to an arbitrary field.

(2) The generic piece that DOES exist (and refutes only the strong reading "from scratch", not the gap as stated): `Tween<T: Lerp>` is a generic data type with `impl Lerp for f32` (tween.rs:45,51,149) and all-`pub` fields + `pub fn value()` / `is_complete()` (tween.rs:151-228,220,228), re-exported via buiy_core::animation (mod.rs:32-36). So an app can attach a `Tween<f32>` and read `.value()` — but the advance/reduced-motion/repeat engine `tick_tween` is PRIVATE (tween.rs), so wiring it to a custom field still requires the app's own `Res<Time>` system exactly as the gap claims. The top-level `buiy` crate re-exports `Tween` but not even `Lerp` (crates/buiy/src/lib.rs:56-58).

(3) No render primitive backs the timer-ring example: searching render/ for arc/conic/ring/sweep/start_angle/end_angle found only linear + radial gradients (instance.rs:348 GRADIENT_KIND_RADIAL, components.rs:78/133 Radial). No conic/arc geometry carries an animatable sweep angle, and RotateTween rotates a whole element (Quat), not an arc's angular extent.

(4) The idiom is confirmed: the progress meter animates via ScaleTween on a left-anchored full-width fill (crates/buiy_widgets/src/composites.rs:26-28,161-236 "never animate a Taffy-owned length per frame"), and the toast entrance via OpacityTween+TranslateTween (examples/buiy_gallery/src/composites.rs:562-567) — every animated value in the codebase is mapped onto one of the five fixed transform/opacity/color targets, never a generic f32 driver.

(5) No MVU tick/Subscription facility exists in THIS tree (HEAD 4010753, pre-MVU-merge): no mvu/state module found under crates/buiy_core/src; and per the gap itself the MVU path would be "recompute fraction from a Timer each frame", not a ready-made tween target.

audit.summary: buiy_widgets ships 12 real marker-driven widgets, each with a `#[require]` contract + a mergeable `bsn!` scene-fn, all folded into `buiy::prelude`: Button, TextInput, Checkbox, Switch, Slider, Disclosure, Dialog (full C5-d open/close/focus-trap/Esc/inert-background), TooltipTrigger, Popover (anchored top-layer + light-dismiss), Menu/MenuButton/MenuItem, and ScrollArea. audit.summary: Buiy ships bevy_picking 0.19's full `Pointer<E>` taxonomy end-to-end: a Buiy AABB/stacking backend (`emit_picks`) feeds `InteractionPlugin`'s hover diff, which emits Over/Out/Move/Press/Release/Click/Drag*/Cancel/Scroll as BOTH observer triggers AND buffered `Messages<Pointer<E>>`, all re-exported through `buiy::prelude`. A drawing loop is fully expressible today: Press = stroke start, Drag = held-move extension (bevy_picking routes Drag to the press-target regardless of current hover, giving in-window pointer "capture" for free), Release/DragEnd = stroke end; canvas-LOCAL (x,y) per sample is `event.pointer_location.position - canvas.GlobalTransform.translation().xy()` — the exact, already-proven pattern the text editor uses. Coords are logical px, sub-pixel f32, and the GlobalTransform basis already folds ancestor scroll, so local coords stay correct even under a scrolled ancestor. The gaps are all non-blocking for this dimension: the backend leaves `HitData.position` unpopulated (app derives local coords itself), there is no OS-level cursor-grab beyond the window edge (deferred, and reachable via bevy directly), and there is no declarative `:hover`/pressed styling model (raw Over/Out + Hovered components are present; visual swaps are app-level). The true blocker for the canvas mechanic is a *drawable render surface*, which belongs to the render dimension, not here.

verdict.gap: Drawable canvas render surface (freehand strokes) — CROSS-DIMENSION, render-owned. Claim: pointer input can sample canvas-local (x,y) but there is no per-pixel/polyline drawing primitive to render accumulated strokes, blocking the Scribbl CANVAS mechanic.
verdict.correction: The audit's core reason — "no per-pixel/polyline drawing primitive to render the accumulated strokes" — is FALSE. A lyon-backed stroked-vector-path render primitive exists and is app-reachable: (1) `Icon` component with a free-form SVG path `d`, `stroke_width`, `size_px`, `fill`, `color` at crates/buiy_core/src/render/components.rs:272, publicly exported via the `buiy` prelude at crates/buiy/src/lib.rs:69; (2) `render::icon_raster::rasterize_icon` at crates/buiy_core/src/render/icon_raster.rs:254 — `parse_path` accepts the full SVG grammar M/L/H/V/C/S/Q/T/A/Z (abs+rel), `tessellate` emits a STROKE with round cap/round join at `stroke_width` (or a non-zero-winding FILL) to an R8 coverage bitmap; (3) `render::icon_producer::extract_buiy_icons` at crates/buiy_core/src/render/icon_producer.rs:193 draws it as a `GlyphAlphaInstance` through the existing coverage.wgsl pipeline (no new GPU code). Accumulated pointer samples can be serialized to `d = "M x0 y0 L x1 y1 L x2 y2 …"` and rendered as a stroked polyline TODAY. RESIDUAL (real but NOT the stated blocker): this is a content-addressed, atlas-cached, rasterize-once vector-ICON path keyed on hash(path_d,stroke_width,size_px,fill) (icon_producer.rs:103) on a fixed 24×24 viewBox uniformly scaled by size_px — designed for ~25 static icons, not LIVE freehand accumulation. A per-frame-growing stroke mints a fresh atlas cell each drag frame (CPU re-tessellate/re-rasterize; old cells grace-evict), so a production canvas wants a direct tessellate-to-quad path instead of the atlas cache. That is an ergonomics/perf gap on top of an EXISTING primitive, not a missing render surface. (Also confirming the input side: `Icon` primitive exists independent of pointer plumbing.)

verdict.evidence: Confirmed the literal field: crates/buiy_core/src/picking/backend.rs:136 passes HitData::new(camera, depth, None, None) (prior agent said line 137 — 1-line drift), so hit.position is None. HitData::new signature is (camera, depth, position: Option<Vec3>, normal: Option<Vec3>) (bevy_picking backend.rs:181), and the field doc says position "may be in any space (World/Screen/Local), specified by the backend" (backend.rs:146). REFUTING evidence: (1) every Pointer<E> carries the public field pointer_location: Location (bevy_picking events.rs:80) whose position: Vec2 (pointer.rs:216) is the window-space pointer point, read directly off the event. (2) Buiy's world-space == window-space: emit_picks compares cursor = loc.position DIRECTLY against gt.translation().truncate() via point_in_node (backend.rs:102, 115-116), so GlobalTransform is in the same space the pointer location is reported in. (3) The cited 'editor pattern' reads press/drag.pointer_location.position directly off the event (crates/buiy_core/src/text/edit/pointer.rs:166,196); its GlobalTransform fold produces entity-LOCAL buffer coords (origin = gt.translation()+content_offset; local = pointer-origin, lines 168,197), a different quantity than the world hit point. In Buiy's flat 2D UI world-space coincides with window-space — crates/buiy_core/src/picking/backend.rs:102,115-116 compares the pointer's loc.position directly against GlobalTransform.translation() — so pointer_location.position (xy) plus hit.depth (z, populated at backend.rs:135-136) fully reconstruct the world-space hit point for every hit, with no GlobalTransform fold. The established editor consumers read exactly this: crates/buiy_core/src/text/edit/pointer.rs:166 (press.pointer_location.position) and :196 (drag.pointer_location.position); their GlobalTransform fold (:168, :197) is to reach node-LOCAL buffer coords, not to recover the world hit point. audit.dimension: Animation (timer ring sweep, spinner, timer color transition, toast fades, hint reveals)
audit.summary: A real, small animation subsystem exists (added by the Widget-Catalog parity work, in this tree): crates/buiy_core/src/animation/ ships a typed Tween<T> engine (from/to/duration/elapsed/easing/repeat), two easing families (Linear + CSS/design cubic-bezier), five wired per-property targets (Translate/Rotate/Scale/Opacity/BackgroundColor), Repeat::{Once,Loop,PingPong} for looping/pulse, and reduced-motion snap-to-rest. AnimationPlugin runs these systems every frame in BuiySet::Animate (before Render, driven by Bevy Time::delta), and the default winit mode is Continuous, so per-frame animation genuinely drives to the GPU. The app CAN drive a per-frame value for opacity/transform/background-color out of the box, and buiy_widgets exposes a left-anchored ScaleTween `meter` (linear progress) and an infinite-ping-pong `pulse_blink`. What is missing is exactly what Scribbl's signature animation needs: there is no arc/ring/dash primitive to PAINT a circular timer sweep, no clean continuous 360 rotation for a spinner, no generic custom-property tween driver (the tick fn is private), no animation sequencing/timeline for transient toasts, and reduced-motion is honored but never sourced from the OS. Note: this tree is main @ 4010753; the MVU core (Tick/Subscription that would feed clock-linked animation thresholds) is NOT present here (it merged later as abb76fb, not an ancestor of HEAD).

verdict.correction: The capability exists on two levels. (1) The game loop itself: every Buiy app IS a Bevy app — examples/hello_button/src/main.rs:13 and examples/buiy_gallery/src/main.rs:31 are `App::new().add_plugins(DefaultPlugins)...run()`, so `Update`, `FixedUpdate`, `Res<Time>`, `Timer`, `Time<Fixed>`, `Time<Virtual>` are all directly in scope (winit rAF supplies the per-frame tick on wasm). The prior agent concedes this base layer. (2) A framework-level timer/tick helper ABOVE raw Bevy Time DOES ship and is promoted into `buiy::prelude`: the animation/tween registry. crates/buiy/src/lib.rs:56 re-exports `Tween, Easing, Repeat, OpacityTween, ...` (and prelude = `pub use crate::*;` at :151). crates/buiy_core/src/animation/tween.rs gives `Tween<T>` with `duration`/`elapsed` (fields ~:150-165), `Tween::secs(...)` (:185), `Repeat::{Once,Loop,PingPong}` for continuous/looping ticks (:101), and `with_on_complete()` (:189) which inserts an `OnComplete` marker (:87) when a countdown completes — the tick engine `tick_tween` at :308 accumulates elapsed by the frame delta and wraps drift-free for repeats. These are advanced per-frame by `advance_*_tweens` systems reading `Res<Time>` (:346+) wired into `BuiySet::Animate` (crates/buiy_core/src/animation/mod.rs:50-63). This maps directly onto Scribbl's needs: the pick(10s)/draw(80s)/reveal(6s) countdowns = `Tween::secs(...).with_on_complete()` observed via the `OnComplete` marker to fire phase transitions; the SVG timer ring depleting over 80s = a value/Opacity/Scale tween's `elapsed`/fraction sampled each frame. An in-tree periodic-timer pattern also exists: `CaretBlink` (crates/buiy_core/src/text/edit/state.rs:54) is a phase-relative blink timer built on `Time::elapsed()`. So there is no genuine missing primitive — the loop + elapsed time + countdown-completion + looping are all present today; only a re-branded general-purpose game `Timer`/fixed-timestep wrapper is absent, and the idiomatic path is to use Bevy's own `Timer`/`Time<Fixed>`/`FixedUpdate` (already reachable) plus the animation helper for the ring.

(c) examples/hello_button/src/main.rs:13 and examples/buiy_gallery/src/main.rs:31 confirm Buiy apps are Bevy apps (DefaultPlugins → winit game loop + Time + Timer + FixedUpdate available directly). buiy::prelude is `pub use crate::*;` (crates/buiy/src/lib.rs:151) and the crate re-exports buiy_bsn::prelude + slices of bevy; downstream apps also `use bevy::prelude::*;` directly, so Bevy's timer/fixed-timestep facilities are in reach. gaps.name: Touch pointer one-frame hover lag breaks cold taps / touch stroke-start
gaps.why: The mobile-stacked variant and any touch drawing rely on pointer down landing on the right node. The picking backend has a documented one-frame hover lag so a press with no prior settled hover (a touch tap, or cold synthetic click) can miss (spec § 6 'Pointer interactivity — touch caveat'). Affects touch canvas stroke-start and mobile seat/tool taps.
gaps.searchedFor: read wasm spec § 6 pointer-interactivity note; referenced picking/backend.rs § 3.3; verified mouse-only interactivity is confirmed
gaps.notes: Invisible for the desktop-mouse MVP (seat-hop solo demo always hovers first). Same lag on native, not web-specific; a real blocker only if Scribbl ships touch. Fix = resolve the press's own-frame location (logged in follow-ups.md). Owned by the input/picking dimension.

verdict.gap: Touch pointer one-frame hover lag breaks cold taps / touch stroke-start
verdict.evidence: The gap's own-named fix — "resolve the press's own-frame location" — already exists as a pub primitive and an established production pattern; the "LACKS the capability" framing is overstated. Searched crates/buiy_core/picking, crates/buiy_widgets, crates/buiy meta-crate, examples, and the wasm spec. Findings: (1) `buiy_core::picking::hit_test(world, point)` [crates/buiy_core/src/picking/mod.rs:117] is a pub stacking-aware synchronous point→topmost-entity hit-test that reads the raw point directly and BYPASSES bevy_picking's hover map — exactly own-frame press-location resolution. (2) It is already production-wired to a press handler: `buiy_widgets::dismiss::press_is_outside` [crates/buiy_widgets/src/dismiss.rs:185] calls hit_test(world, point) to resolve what is under a press independent of the hover map. (3) `Pointer<Press>` carries its own current-frame location `press.pointer_location.position`, consumed directly for caret placement by `editor_pointer_press` [crates/buiy_core/src/text/edit/pointer.rs:166]; a canvas stroke-start reads the identical field, so the stroke START coordinate is never hover-lagged. (4) Touch is not unwired: BuiyPlugin adds bevy_picking `PointerInputPlugin` [crates/buiy/src/lib.rs:253] (native winit touch → PointerInput with PointerId::Touch) and `emit_picks` is pointer-id-agnostic, iterating all (PointerId, PointerLocation) pairs [crates/buiy_core/src/picking/backend.rs:88], so touch pointers already produce PointerHits→Pointer<E>. RESIDUAL (real, documented, spec-tracked in wasm spec §6 + picking/backend.rs §3.3, lines 22-27): only the AUTOMATIC hover-map-derived press.entity used by the built-in Pointer<Click>→OnPress widget activation [crates/buiy_core/src/picking/activation.rs:62] carries the one-frame lag; a cold tap with no prior settled hover can mis-target via that convenience path. But an app (Scribbl) can already land cold taps/strokes correctly today using the existing pub APIs — what is deferred is only auto-wiring hit_test into that convenience path for touch-first UX, not a missing capability.
verdict.correction: EXISTS. Primitive: `buiy_core::picking::hit_test(world: &World, point: Vec2) -> Option<Entity>` at crates/buiy_core/src/picking/mod.rs:117 — pub, re-exported at buiy_core::picking::hit_test, stacking-aware (same global_paint_order/painters_z derivation as emit_picks), reads the raw point and bypasses the hover map, i.e. resolves a press's own-frame target. Established pattern: buiy_widgets::dismiss::press_is_outside at crates/buiy_widgets/src/dismiss.rs:185 already calls hit_test on a press point in production. Press location: Pointer<Press>.pointer_location.position (current-frame, never lagged) used at crates/buiy_core/src/text/edit/pointer.rs:166 — a canvas stroke-start reads the same field. Touch plumbing: bevy_picking PointerInputPlugin added at crates/buiy/src/lib.rs:253 + pointer-id-agnostic emit_picks at crates/buiy_core/src/picking/backend.rs:88. The one-frame lag affects only the built-in hover-map-derived Pointer<Click>→OnPress auto-activation (crates/buiy_core/src/picking/activation.rs:62), which an app need not depend on for stroke-start or custom tap handling.

gaps.name: No browser accessibility sink on web
gaps.why: On wasm Buiy builds its AccessKit TreeUpdate but reaches no browser AT (spec D8) — a11y tree is data-ready but the web sink is absent. Not required by the Scribbl brief, but means the web build is not screen-reader accessible.

verdict.gap: No browser accessibility sink on web: on wasm Buiy builds its AccessKit TreeUpdate but reaches no browser assistive technology (no accesskit_web/DOM sink).
verdict.evidence: Searched the full working tree and could not refute the gap. (1) The only a11y sink is AccessKitAdapterPlugin (crates/buiy_core/src/a11y/adapter.rs:39-82), which is winit-only: it imports bevy::winit::accessibility::ACCESS_KIT_ADAPTERS (adapter.rs:29) and pushes each frame's TreeUpdate into that thread-local (adapter.rs:76-81 with_borrow_mut loop calling adapter.update_if_active). On wasm accesskit_winit has no web backend, so the slot holds a null/no-op adapter and the push is inert. (2) grep for accesskit_web / DOM sink / ARIA-overlay across crates/ and examples/ returns nothing; the only a11y crate deps (Cargo.toml:91-103) are accesskit 0.24, accesskit_winit 0.32, accesskit_consumer 0.36 — no web/canvas adapter. (3) The web examples wire no custom sink: examples/buiy_web/src/main.rs is canvas-bound Window + BuiyPlugin only, and examples/{buiy_web,gallery_web}/index.html carry a bare <canvas id=buiy> with no aria/role/hidden-DOM. (4) The translate layer (crates/buiy_core/src/a11y/translate.rs:2) is intentionally winit-free pure data — tree is web-ready, sink is not. This is a deliberately-staged, documented gap: wasm spec D8 (docs/specs/2026-06-25-buiy-wasm-browser-support-design.md:96-102, 148 'A11y gate (blocked upstream)') states web builds the TreeUpdate but 'reaches no browser assistive technology — AccessKit ships no web/canvas adapter. Staged and disclosed.' Prior-art corroborates (docs/prior-art/web-rendering/lessons.md:13 'Only the sink is missing, not the tree'; accessibility.md:22; open-problems.md:7-9; accesskit/lessons.md:41 'No accesskit_web crate exists on crates.io'). The prior agent's file:line anchor (crates/buiy/src/lib.rs:259 AccessKitAdapterPlugin is winit-only) is accurate.

audit.dimension: Text specifics (letter-slot boxes, mono, letter-spacing, big display)
audit.summary: Buiy's landed text stack (T1-T9 + editing E1-E6) already carries every atomic text knob Scribbl's screens need, and the parity gallery exercises the exact combination (named monospace + LetterSpacing + uppercase headers). Monospace is first-class: GenericFamily::Monospace re-pins to an embedded true-monospace face (Geist Mono variable), and apps can also reach it by name or register their own .ttf/.otf. LetterSpacing, per-entity TextColor/FontWeight/FontSize, TextAlign::Center, and a single-line editable text input all exist and are in the buiy prelude. The only real absences are CSS text-transform (uppercasing a code input must be done app-side) and author-controlled inline rich-text (mixed color/weight within ONE Text node), both of which have clean app-level workarounds and neither blocks a Scribbl text screen.
